title: Review of Systems Hub
examInfo: Two Canvas mock board exams of 200 questions each, INBDE style, with images and patient boxes. You get 200 minutes once you start.
Mock 1: Thursday, December 3. Mock 2: Thursday, December 10. Both 8:00 am to noon CST: start at 8:00 am, finish once you start; Canvas closes the exam at noon.
Remote, on Canvas with Respondus LockDown Browser and Monitor. Use a stable internet connection: the exams have images and patient boxes.
Pass/fail: complete the course's 8 quizzes and score 55% or better over the two mocks together (220 of 400).

Head & Neck Anatomy, Dental Anatomy & Occlusion, Fundamentals I and II, Oral Microbiology, Neuroscience, the systems courses (Cardio & Respiratory, Renal, Heme & Endo, MSK & GI), Ethics & Professionalism, Evidence-Based Dentistry, Radiology and Emergencies in the Dental Clinic.
The course hasn't said how many questions come from each course. This hub's mock spreads its 200 by the size of each course: a guess, not the exam's blueprint.
Self-study, November 16 to December 11, with no review sessions. Your earlier lecturers will answer questions if you ask them.

Each course is a section, cut into parts you can do in a sitting: high-yield notes, a Plain English version, a cram list and board-style questions. Built from the class's study guides, answered objectives and notes, the class above's, and this site's earlier hubs. Nothing from this course's quizzes.

likelyTopics.t: Horner syndrome: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis and flushing from a cervical sympathetic lesion
Nerves at risk in thyroid surgery and the carotid sheath and its neighbors
Root of the neck: subclavian branches, phrenic nerve, thoracic duct and the superior thoracic aperture
Posterior triangle: CN XI and the cervical plexus at the nerve point
Suprahyoid and infrahyoid nerves, landmarks, carotid sinus and fascial spaces
Foramina of the skull and what passes through each (rotundum, ovale, spinosum, jugular foramen)
Cavernous sinus: contents, drainage and thrombosis with CN VI as the first sign
Cranial nerve lesions: III palsy, tongue and uvula deviation, UMN vs LMN facial weakness, corneal reflex
Epidural vs subdural vs subarachnoid bleeds
Visual pathway lesions and skull bones
Parotid: what runs through it, the duct opposite the maxillary second molar, IX–otic–auriculotemporal secretion, Frey syndrome
Facial nerve branches, Bell palsy and facial paralysis from a misplaced inferior alveolar block
Orbit: blow-out fracture, extraocular muscle actions and nerves, accommodation and glaucoma
Sensory supply of the face, scalp layers and lacrimal secretion
Muscles of mastication: actions, the lateral pterygoid as the opener, jaw deviation toward a V3 lesion
V3 branches, the chorda tympani on the lingual nerve, and the anatomy and complications of dental blocks
TMJ structure, compartments, dislocation and nerve supply
Maxillary artery parts and fossa boundaries
Converting between Universal, Palmer and FDI, permanent and primary
Eruption ages and sequences: primary central-lateral-first molar-canine-second molar; maxillary 6-1-2-4-5-3-7-8, mandibular 6-1-2-3-4-5-7-8
Primary versus permanent teeth, and the one-of-a-kind primary teeth
Calcification and root completion timelines; succedaneous teeth
Heights of contour on each surface, and what over- and undercontouring do
Canines: longest tooth, root and crown; maxillary versus mandibular canine features
Contact, embrasure and CEJ trends and their exceptions
Telling the incisors apart: maxillary lateral traits, mandibular central versus lateral, the cingulum
Molar roots and canals: palatal > MB > DB, MB2, the mesial root of mandibular molars, and the furcation levels
Premolar identification: maxillary first (two roots, mesial concavity), mandibular first (canine-like, marginal ridge), mandibular second (Y, H, U)
Maxillary molar crowns: cusp sizes, oblique ridge, Carabelli, lingual width; first versus second molar
Mandibular molars: five versus four cusps, grooves, smallest and tallest cusps
Fusion, gemination and concrescence (the tooth count), supernumerary and missing teeth
Hereditary versus acquired enamel and dentin defects: amelogenesis and dentinogenesis imperfecta, fluorosis, tetracycline, Turner tooth
Tooth identification, right or left included
Shape and root anomalies: taurodontism, enamel pearl, dilaceration, talon cusp, dens in dente, Hutchinson incisors
Attrition, abrasion, erosion and abfraction
Collagen: Gly-X-Y, the triple helix, vitamin C–dependent hydroxylation and the collagen diseases (scurvy, osteogenesis imperfecta)
Hemoglobin: cooperativity, T and R states, the Bohr effect, 2,3-BPG and fetal hemoglobin
Amino acid side chains (histidine's pKa) and the levels of protein structure
Carbohydrate isomers, sucrose and S. mutans, GAGs and glycation
Lipid structure, base pairing and buffers
Phases of the nerve action potential, refractory periods, and how hyperkalemia, tetrodotoxin and local anesthetics change it
Transport mechanisms and osmosis: passive, primary and secondary active transport, tonicity, the reflection coefficient
Nernst equilibrium potentials (a tenfold gradient gives about 60 mV) and the resting potential
Synapses, the main neurotransmitters, and the neuromuscular junction (botulinum, myasthenia gravis)
Organelle functions and address tags, the cytoskeleton, and apoptosis
Modes of inheritance, pedigree clues and carrier risk (the 2/3 rule)
Oncogenes versus tumor suppressors (two hits), p53, RB, BRCA and HPV, and benign versus malignant
Replication enzymes, leading and lagging strands, and telomerase
Transcription: σ and promoters, the lac operon, the three eukaryotic polymerases and epigenetic switches
RNA processing, translation and the types of mutation
Necrosis patterns and the organ or disease each belongs to (coagulative infarct, liquefactive brain and abscess, caseous TB, fat necrosis pancreas, fibrinoid vessels)
Apoptosis versus necrosis, and the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways
Acute inflammation: exudate, leukocyte recruitment steps; chronic inflammation: M1 and M2 macrophages
Repair and scar problems (granulation tissue, keloid versus hypertrophic scar) and acute-phase proteins
Tumor naming, benign versus malignant, grade versus stage
Human herpesviruses HHV-1 to HHV-8: diseases and latency sites, with their oral lesions
Hepatitis A to E (spread, chronicity, prevention) and hepatitis B serology
HIV: entry through CD4 and CCR5 or CXCR4, the life cycle, stages by CD4 count and tests
Oncogenic viruses: HPV E6 and E7, EBV, HBV and HCV, HTLV-1, HHV-8
RNA viruses: measles and Koplik spots, influenza drift and shift, rabies, enveloped versus naked
Gram-positive versus gram-negative envelope and the gram stain
Exotoxins versus endotoxin and the classic toxins (cholera, Shiga, tetanus, botulinum, staph)
S. aureus virulence, abscess and MRSA; S. epidermidis biofilm; S. pneumoniae capsule
Gene transfer, growth curve and the three ways to make ATP
Gram-negative rods, MacConkey agar and the periodontal red complex
The cranial nerves: jobs, parasympathetic ganglia and lesion signs (tongue, jaw, uvula, eye)
Spinal cord tracts, blood supply and cord syndromes (Brown-Séquard, anterior cord)
The intracranial bleeds and the cavernous sinus
Brainstem rule of 4 and the medullary syndromes
Neural tube and neural crest derivatives and their defects
Stroke territories: ACA, MCA, PCA, lacunar and brainstem syndromes
Upper versus lower motor neuron signs and the neuromuscular diseases
The trigeminal sensory nuclei and VPM
DCML versus spinothalamic pathway and where each crosses
Basal ganglia pathways, Parkinson and Huntington disease; cerebellar signs
Local anesthetic mechanism and the properties that set onset, potency and duration
Ester versus amide metabolism and allergy; prilocaine and articaine
Local anesthetic systemic toxicity
Resting potential, the action potential and myelin
Synaptic transmission, receptors, NMDA; general anesthetic action, MAC and sedation levels
Trigeminal neuralgia and the upper- versus lower-half causes of head and facial pain
Pain fibers, gate control, sensitization; nociceptive versus neuropathic pain and their drugs
Taste and smell pathways and tongue innervation
Visual field defects, eye-movement nerves and INO
Autonomic layout and transmitters; hearing; facial trauma
Clearance: the formula, inulin = GFR, PAH = RPF, creatinine and GFR, and clearance ratios
Afferent versus efferent arteriole resistance, angiotensin II, prostaglandins and autoregulation
Body fluid compartments (60–40–20), plasma osmolarity, fluid shifts and IV fluids
Filtration barrier and juxtaglomerular apparatus
What each segment reabsorbs and which transporter and diuretic belong to it
Glucose transport maximum, glycosuria and SGLT2 inhibitors
Countercurrent multiplication, urea recycling and ADH's actions
SIADH, central and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and ADH control
Reading a blood gas: the four simple disorders and their compensation
Potassium shifts and the drugs that raise or lower K+
PTH, calcitriol and FGF23, and ANP versus RAAS
CKD stages, causes, azotemia versus uremia, and CKD mineral and bone disorder
Nephritic versus nephrotic syndrome and the classic glomerular diseases
Pyelonephritis, casts, stones and renal tumors
Dialysis patient: timing after dialysis, the fistula arm, bleeding and hepatitis
Drug choice and dosing in kidney failure (analgesics, antibiotics, local anesthetics)
Diuretic classes, sites and side effects
Oral and radiographic signs of kidney failure
The patient on long-term steroids in the chair: a suppressed axis, the adrenal crisis and 100 mg hydrocortisone, and why steroids are tapered
Cushing vs Addison by the labs: cortisol read with ACTH, and the oral pigmentation of Addison disease
Growth hormone regulation, IGF-1, and acromegaly's growing jaw (Class III, diastemas, macroglossia)
Corticosteroid choice and side effects: fludrocortisone vs dexamethasone, candidiasis, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis
Pituitary adenomas and the posterior pituitary: prolactinoma, bitemporal hemianopsia, diabetes insipidus vs SIADH; the adrenal zones and Conn syndrome
Reading TSH and free T4: Graves (TSH low, T4 high) vs Hashimoto (TSH high, T4 low), and titrating levothyroxine by TSH
Thyroid drugs: levothyroxine's rules, methimazole vs propylthiouracil in pregnancy, agranulocytosis, what methimazole blocks
Hyperthyroid vs hypothyroid in the chair: epinephrine caution and thyroid storm; macroglossia and delayed healing
Primary vs secondary hyperparathyroidism and hypoparathyroidism by their labs; lamina dura and brown tumors on the radiograph
Thyroid carcinomas: papillary (lymphatics), follicular (invasion, blood), medullary (C cells, RET, MEN 2)
Hypoglycemia in the chair: the signs, the sulfonylurea or insulin with a skipped meal, oral glucose if awake, glucagon if not
Which drugs cause hypoglycemia and weight gain (insulin and the secretagogues) and which don't; metformin's rules
Drug classes by mechanism and adverse effect: SGLT2 (yeast infections), GLP-1 (weight loss, C-cell warning), DPP-4, TZD (heart failure), the insulins
Type 1 vs type 2, C-peptide, HbA1c cutoffs and control before implants
Insulin release through the K-ATP channel, and diabetes in the mouth with its two-way periodontal link
The GI hormones: cell, trigger and actions of gastrin, CCK, secretin, GIP/GLP-1 and motilin
Digestion and absorption: monosaccharide carriers, micelles and chylomicrons, bile salt recycling and where B12 is absorbed
Parietal cell acid secretion: the H+/K+ pump, its three stimulants, its brakes and the vagal cephalic phase
Motility: slow waves, the migrating motor complex and motilin, and achalasia
Saliva: isotonic primary saliva made hypotonic by the ducts, and dual autonomic control
Foregut, midgut and hindgut: arteries, boundaries, the stomach's arteries, referred pain and retroperitoneal organs
Portal-caval anastomoses in portal hypertension: esophageal varices, caput medusae, rectal varices
Abdominal wall layers and the arcuate line, inguinal hernias (MDs don't LIe), dermatomes and diaphragm openings
GI histology by region: esophagus, stomach cells, duodenum vs jejunum vs ileum vs colon, oral mucosa and salivary glands
Liver histology: the acinus zones, Kupffer and stellate cells, and the gallbladder wall
Peptic ulcer disease: H. pylori and NSAIDs, and the acid drugs (PPIs vs H2 blockers, antacid chelation, misoprostol)
Liver disease: hepatitis viruses, hemochromatosis and Wilson disease, acetaminophen, and the cirrhotic dental patient (INR, platelets, analgesics)
Crohn disease vs ulcerative colitis and celiac disease, with their oral findings
Antiemetics (5-HT3, D2, H1, muscarinic), antidiarrheals and laxatives
GERD and Barrett esophagus, colorectal syndromes with oral signs, and C. difficile colitis
Efficacy versus effectiveness, the study-context continuum and the three evidence-to-practice gaps
Pre-appraised evidence: literature review, systematic review, meta-analysis and guideline; the pyramid; GRADE and AGREE
Naming the design from a study description, and what case-control and cohort studies are each good for
The 5 A's in order and building a PICO(T) question; question types and their best designs
Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values: calculating them and choosing a test for screening or confirming
Reading relative risk, odds ratio, hazard ratio and NNT with their confidence intervals and p-values; type I and II errors and power
Internal and external validity; bias, confounding and chance; randomization, blinding and intention-to-treat
Standardization, calibration and reliability; precision versus accuracy
